name: October
summary: October brings daytime family Halloween events and nighttime haunts on park-specific dates. Weekend demand is often high; some haunts also run on weekdays.

verdict.short: October offers the widest Halloween selection, with family events by day and haunts on selected nights. Check the date and ticket rules.
bestFor: Haunt nights — the season's best product
worstFor: The last two Saturdays at the big parks

crowds.shape: Haunt nights and family days follow different schedules. Selected weekday events also draw crowds, while many weekend dates are busy.
peakWindows: The last two Saturdays before Halloween
quietWindows: Some non-event weekdays, where the park is open

cost.note: Ticket prices move by date at every park on this site; the level describes the month's overall shape rather than any single day.

planningNotes.heading: The month in one decision
body: The October split is extreme: weekday day-park visits run near-walk-on while haunt Saturdays are the year's biggest crowds. Knowing which you are buying is the month's whole plan.

planningNotes.heading: The detail that matters
body: The northern parks add holiday-season hours late in the month; Great America's October weekends are among the best atmosphere days on this site.

freshness.sourceNote: Crowd and cost shapes describe multi-year patterns across the ten parks rather than a forecast for any single year. Weather figures are climate normals for each region and do not decay; the Texas figures blend the DFW and San Antonio areas, and the Southern California figures blend the coastal and inland valleys.
